title: Obs Console triage — daily log
content:
2026-03-13 notes (quick scratchpad)

Morning summary:
- Two customer-facing incidents flagged overnight: Acme Payments (CS-9012) reported dashboard widgets failing to load; BetaShop (CS-9041) saw stale latency percentiles.
- Pager: spike 02:14→02:27 UTC, PG1 autoscaler looped, mem pressure on node pool r-prod-gpu-1.

High-level hypothesis:
- Widget rendering error seems tied to new panel plugin version (v2.1.0) rolled to canary last week. Plugin fetch failures -> blank frames.
- Stale percentiles likely aggregation lag due to Prometheus remote-write retry backlog during the autoscaler churn.

Immediate actions (today):
1) Reproduce Acme widget failure locally
   - Open Grafana console with test user (impersonate acme-readonly) -> http request to plugin endpoint times out (~3s)
   - Steps recorded: Network tab shows 504 at /plugins/com.redwood-panel/v2/data?range=...
   - TODO: try pinning plugin to v2.0.7 on staging instance and validate.
2) Confirm BetaShop percentiles
   - Check prom write queue length 02:00-03:00 UTC: spike from 0.1% -> 18% backlog (alerts suppressed during maintenance window?)
   - Action: escalate to infra SRE (tag @Luca) to inspect remote-write connections and tail logs for backoff.
3) Follow-ups for CS and AE
   - DM CS lead (Marta) with TL;DR + ETA for fix. Draft message: "We have a reproducer and a mitigation (pin plugin). Will test rollback on staging and schedule ~30m window for prod revert. Will update in 90m."
   - Add note to CS ticket CS-9012: reproduction steps + link to PR that pins plugin.

Investigations details / scratchy repro notes:
- Repro on staging: yes, intermittent (3/10 loads) -> likely race when plugin requests metadata from inference-console backend.
- Backend logs show 502 at the plugin-proxy layer around same timestamps. Trace id: trace-20260312-AB12.
- Pending check: is plugin-proxy running latest sidecar (https://github.com/redwood-inference/plugin-proxy/commit/4f3b2a)? Sidecar config change in that commit introduced a shorter connection timeout (1s) which could cause 504s under load.

Mitigation plan (short-term):
- Pin panel plugin to v2.0.7 on canary/staging and run smoke for 2 hrs. If stable, schedule a rollback for prod tomorrow 03:00 UTC (low traffic).
- Update rollout policy in console to add a canary stage with 5% hosts for panel plugin changes (notes for product: request small change to rollout UI).

Longer-term follow-ups (in backlog):
- Make plugin-proxy timeouts configurable per plugin (ticket JIRA-OBS-4199).
- Add a Grafana dashboard alert for sudden increase in plugin fetch latencies (currently hidden under generic 5xx).
- Add automated smoke test that loads core dashboard frames in staging after plugin releases.

Open questions / things to verify:
- Was there any other team that bumped plugin version? Check PR history and owners (Priya recently approved UI plugin PRs).
- Does the autoscaler flapping correlate with a maintenance cron job? Check infra calendar for 02:00 UTC jobs.
- Should we temporarily disable the new plugin rollout until we have rollout UI change? Probably yes if customers impacted >1.

Quick todo checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] Pin plugin on staging (Aisha)
- [ ] Ask infra to validate remote-write (Luca)
- [ ] Draft prod rollback schedule and sync with oncall (Priya)
- [ ] Update CS ticket and DM customer (Marta contact)
- [ ] Open JIRA-OBS-4199 and assign to eng-observability

Random notes to self:
- Remember to export the Grafana panel HTTP traces and attach to JIRA (use trace-20260312-AB12).
- Keep the canary window docs updated in Confluence (link: confluence.redwood.internal/display/OBS/Release+Rollouts).

Session end — will update after staging pin test.

---
Revision log (for my own sanity):
- 2026-03-12 18:04 UTC: initial triage notes + links
- 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC: repro confirmed on staging, added mitigation plan
- 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC: notified CS, awaiting infra check

Inline references: JIRA-OBS-4123 (Acme widget failure), CS-9012 (Acme customer ticket), CS-9041 (BetaShop).

End of file.
